scenarios.title: A restore keeps canonical URLs and fences every prior-epoch token

requirements.selectedText: Restoring the same logical Scope therefore preserves its canonical Scope and Resource URLs while rejecting every history-dependent token from the prior epoch.

scenarios.title: A prior-epoch key is unbound under the new epoch and executes anew, never as a replay

requirements.selectedText: A new epoch is a new namespace: a key first used under a prior epoch is unbound, and a retry under the new epoch executes as a new mutation, which a client that observes a changed `scopeEpoch` MUST treat as a first execution rather than a replay.

scenarios.title: Alias singletons use durable one-entry receipts with the ordinary key and replay rules

requirements.selectedText:
A singleton `put-alias` or `delete-alias` on a Transactional Scope is a
one-operation Mutation Transaction.

scenarios.title: Alias changes occupy no Scope position and appear in no Event, change group or snapshot

requirements.selectedText:
Alias mutations occupy no Scope position, induce no Event, and appear in
no change group or snapshot.

scenarios.title: Alias operations are excluded from atomic batch membership

requirements.selectedText:
`batch` admits no alias
operation, so atomic create-plus-alias is unavailable.

scenarios.title: An expired creation projects the disclosed identity or exactly withheld true

requirements.selectedText:
A completed Resource creation's expired projection MUST carry exactly one of
these forms; every other operation's expired projection MUST omit `allocated`

scenarios.title: Withheld allocation preserves internal binding and independently authorizes every dependent

requirements.selectedText:
Each dependent still undergoes ordinary
current authorization independently.

scenarios.title: Only already admitted caught-up streams in views receiving the erasure cross its atomic publication fence

requirements.selectedText:
Only such caught-up streams in a view receiving the erasure record receive the
complete group at P; their server-side stream position then advances to P.

scenarios.title: Reconnect uses the atomically applied durable checkpoint and resnapshots when it precedes erasure

requirements.selectedText:
The client advances its durable checkpoint
only after atomically applying the complete group.

scenarios.title: Atomic all-member admission preserves unresolved creator attempts and immutable terminal bindings

requirements.selectedText: When a sequence member depends on an authority-allocated creation whose identity is not yet committed, admission MUST durably reserve that member's key and pending receipt together with all other unknown member keys in the same atomic admission step.
Its unresolved dependency form pins each reference to the particular creator attempt and operation slot, not merely to a reusable key or the spelling of a label.
The authority MUST preserve enough pinned resolution state to resolve or retract every dependent even if the creator's failed receipt is later forgotten and its key reused.
A terminal dependent's normalized identity is immutable: a later creator attempt cannot rebind it.
Atomic admission does not combine the sequence's separately committing member executions into one transaction.
When its creator commits, the authority atomically records the binding fact with the creator's effects and terminal disposition; a dependent resolves only against that pinned fact.

On a later presentation of the dependent, a successful new creator supplies an identity that conflicts with the retained unbound marker; another permanent creator failure normalizes to the same unbound marker when the remaining fields match.
Binding, retraction, and commit check the same exclusive attempt ownership; a stale execution cannot resolve or commit a replacement attempt's work

scenarios.title: Direct unresolved comparison uses a separate finite wait, proven conflict or receipt, and retryable 503 at its deadline

requirements.selectedText: A direct singleton or batch that encounters an unresolved reservation MUST reject an already provable semantic mismatch with `409` `idempotency-conflict`.
Otherwise it MUST wait for comparison to become possible, within one finite authority-selected comparison budget.
This budget is separate from `transaction.duration`, which bounds admitted execution;
Until equality is established, this caller MUST NOT receive the owner's pending receipt, execute a second mutation, or retract the owner's reservation.
If comparison remains unresolved at the deadline, return direct `503` `temporarily-unavailable` with `retry: after-delay`; the response SHOULD carry `Retry-After` when a useful delay is known.
Once the reservation resolves, ordinary canonical comparison returns the existing receipt or the conflict.

If the Scope epoch changes, the authority MUST stop this waiting comparison or admission attempt with that same `503`; the client must refresh Scope discovery and present a fresh request before competing in the new epoch.

scenarios.title: A waiting direct request may win fresh admission in the same epoch without inheriting ownership or resetting its deadline

requirements.selectedText: If that unresolved reservation is retracted while the explicit direct request is waiting, the request MAY compete for fresh admission in the same Scope epoch, under current authorization and within the same overall finite deadline.
It executes only after winning a new reservation for its own request; it inherits neither the previous attempt's ownership, receipt identity, nor unresolved dependency form.
Retraction or a change of owner MUST NOT reset the deadline.

If the Scope epoch changes, the authority MUST stop this waiting comparison or admission attempt with that same `503`; the client must refresh Scope discovery and present a fresh request before competing in the new epoch.

scenarios.title: Persistent Event consumers claiming protocol-backed erasure handling integrate Scope changefeed and snapshot ledger recovery and cleanup

requirements.selectedText: A persistent Event consumer claiming protocol-backed erasure handling MUST integrate the existing Scope changefeed and snapshot erasure ledger as its supported acquisition and reconciliation route.

It applies projected erasure records to its retained copies and, for this changefeed/ledger integration, follows the existing durable-checkpoint, disconnect, replay-expiry, and Authorization View recovery rules, including a fresh snapshot and its ledger when required.
This requirement scopes the supported erasure-handling claim; it neither prohibits other storage deployments nor exempts any store, cache, or replica from the every-store erasure duty.

scenarios.title: Snapshot GET/HEAD retrieves the same valid manifest without replacing its anchor or renewing expiry

requirements.selectedText: The manifest's `id` MUST support GET and HEAD while the snapshot handle remains valid.
GET retrieves the same manifest, including its identity, anchor, checkpoint, expiry, erasure ledger, and initial stream pages; it MUST NOT create a replacement snapshot or extend `expiresAt`.

scenarios.title: Snapshot handle expiry and non-disclosure precede conditionals and never disguise a pre-expiry service failure

requirements.selectedText: An authorized expired or no-longer-available snapshot handle returns `410 cursor-expired`; an unknown or undisclosable target retains uniform `404 resource-not-found`.
Actual service inability before the promised expiry is a service failure, not an expiration diagnosis

scenarios.title: Issued receipt-page URLs preserve boundaries across same-epoch restart while detail remains available

requirements.selectedText: An already issued receipt-page URL MUST remain usable across ordinary restart or failover in the same Scope epoch while the receipt detail remains available, preserving its recorded entry boundaries and applying current authorization and erasure projection.
This preserves detail expiry, failed-receipt forgetting, retraction, and prior-epoch non-disclosure.

scenarios.title: Unacceptable successful response media yields bodyless 406 before admission while ordinary refusals retain precedence

requirements.selectedText: In every profile, an otherwise valid request whose `Accept` field accepts none of the endpoint's successful response media types MUST receive a bodyless `406 Not Acceptable`, with no BDP problem code, family, or retry member.
For a new mutation submission this refusal occurs before durable admission, key binding, receipt creation, or state change.

scenarios.title: Receipt and page responses omit optional validators while retaining private no-store and HTTP preconditions

requirements.selectedText: Receipt and receipt-page representations MUST omit `ETag` and `Last-Modified` initially and retain `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

scenarios.title: Finite changes and Event pages omit optional validators without changing cursor semantics or adding SSE group validators

requirements.selectedText: Finite Scope changefeed pages and finite Event pages, both Scope `events/` and Resource `view=events`, MUST omit `ETag` and `Last-Modified` initially.
SSE has no per-group HTTP validator or new group-addressing URL

scenarios.title: Read conditionals preserve ordinary refusal precedence and produce native bodyless 304 or 412 without checkpoint advancement

requirements.selectedText: Normal authentication, authorization/non-disclosure, query and cursor checks, Scope epoch/view and minimum-position checks, and erasure/expiry checks MUST precede any conditional not-modified shortcut.
Omitting optional validators does not permit ignoring HTTP preconditions.
A `304` is not delivery or application of a change group or erasure record and MUST NOT advance a client's durable checkpoint.

scenarios.title: HEAD preserves GET decisions and required metadata and ends without bodies or SSE frames

requirements.selectedText: HEAD retains the corresponding GET authorization, query, cursor, media negotiation, and precondition decision and MUST send no response body.
For an acceptable SSE representation, HEAD returns the corresponding response metadata and ends without SSE frames; it MUST NOT remain open merely to stream events.
